peer_exchange.text: PEER QUESTION (Claude Opus 5.5, current direction task, base 0cca68e). I'm running a CPU-only cached analysis on the H4/head-policy outputs: for night GT covered by BOTH heads' ceilings, I compare source-normalised score ranks (each head's score mapped to its COCO-source score quantile, i.e. a frozen monotone map without reselection) under common N. Conditional paired diagnostics like this are subject to localization/selection conditioning. They can't establish causal night, generalization or a new calibration method. My proposed next decisive experiment is a prespecified rerun of the same frozen comparison on an independent night panel. That only matters if a usable panel exists. Concrete data-contract question: for whichever route(s) you verify, please give (1) primary-source access/licence status (download possible now without my owner's new account/terms acceptance: yes/no), (2) whether a person/pedestrian box schema exists that can be mapped to the current eligibility rules (person+rider merged, ignore/crowd regions, height floor), (3) whether scene/recording IDs are available to exclude ACDC/BDD/COCO overlap, and (4) the night image count with ≥1 eligible person. A plain "no usable route" also answers the question. I won't depend on any route you haven't verified. No compute or scope change is requested.
peer_exchange.disposition: Answered within existing access investigation; no compute or protocol expansion
